title: LLM Routing Layer — LiteLLM, OpenRouter, Portkey

questions.question: One model handles every request: simple triage burns money, and a provider outage stops everything. What is the structural fix?
options: Buy a bigger quota on the same model
Stop doing triage entirely
Hardcode a second model into every call site
Route per request by cost and need, with aliases and fallback chains
questions.explanation: One model for everything wastes money and fails as one unit. This lesson builds the routing layer: aliases, fallbacks, and per-request choice.

questions.question: What model chain does the fast alias select?
options: openai/gpt-4o -> anthropic/claude-sonnet
anthropic/claude-sonnet -> google/gemini-pro
anthropic/claude-haiku -> openai/gpt-4o
openai/gpt-4o-mini -> anthropic/claude-haiku
questions.explanation: The fast route starts with openai/gpt-4o-mini and falls back to anthropic/claude-haiku.

questions.question: What happens to an SSN in messages before provider_call?
options: redacts to [REDACTED]; redacted=True
It is sent unchanged to every fallback
It is hashed but still shown in the prompt
It causes routing to fail before any attempt
questions.explanation: redact_pii replaces the SSN pattern (and card pattern) before the provider request, and the invocation records that redaction occurred.

questions.question: What result does route return when every provider in an alias chain is in OUTAGE?
options: The last provider's stale response
all providers failed
A successful empty completion
A 403 scope error
questions.explanation: Each provider failure is recorded; if none succeeds, the invocation returns the explicit all-providers-failed error.

questions.question: How is a successful invocation cost computed?
options: By counting only prompt characters
As a flat fee per route
token rates per million applied to usage
By using the number of fallback attempts as dollars
questions.explanation: The pricing table is per million tokens, so route combines prompt and completion usage with the selected model's input/output rates.

questions.question: Why does the route alias help the application?
options: It makes every provider return identical hidden states
It removes the need to measure latency
It guarantees the first provider is always available
alias owns selection and fallback
questions.explanation: Aliases decouple the caller from concrete provider names, allowing routing, outage fallback, and pricing policy to change centrally.
